comments.text:
👕 Merch → https://scryleus.store/

WATCH NEXT:  
Why I Stopped Caring About Work → https://youtu.be/y8fHE6qRiQ8
You got the same response from all 7 AIs, because all read the same information in the internet

I think you touched on the answer a long time ago, you dont need a job, you need an income. The 9 to 5 is a trap as it cuts off all other possibilities and outcomes by making you think you are safe. From experience you are not safe, you are just trapped in a loop which stifles creativity and causes anxiety until the day comes when you are no longer required.

LLMs make it sound so easy: learn high-value skills, master sales, and land B2B clients—all on top of a 9-to-5. They completely gloss over the massive risk, burnout, and brutal reality of landing clients with zero experience or connections.
"you havent really moved, youve just upgraded the cage" damn this hit me right in the feels. In the process of downsizing my lifestyle. I want my time back.

I learned how to escape the 9-5, 38 years ago. I started investing 10% of my income every month for 29 years. I retired at 57 in 2018 with $1.8M and 10 years of deferred income at $123K per year which has allowed the $1.8M grow to $2.9M….that said, once I retired I entered the world of elder care. I cared for my mother from 2018 until 2022 and now I started caring for my 90 yr old 2nd cousin January 2023. He’s now 93. I’m his last living relative. I have not done the things I had hoped to do but hey, it’s family. The bright spot is my 2nd cousin is leaving me his $1.5M brokerage account. I will use a portion of that to convert my IRA to ROTH. My 66 year old sister (single no children) called last month and said she’s been diagnosed with early onset Alzheimer’s…….😢…….I’m now 65 and I’m exhausted.
Move to the woods and be a hermit.  Boom.
I ESCAPED the 9 to 5 for a 6 to 6...

We need income generating assets. Multiple of them.

All the best everyone.

Good video, and the "keep your job, build something on the side" advice is sound. But I think you skipped the hardest part — the "million dollar question" you mentioned yourself: How do you find that skill?

I retired at 56 after decades of work, saving, and planning (while the rollercoaster of life and time did its thing). No hack or shortcut. And when I finally stopped working, it might have even looked like luck from the outside. But my god — it wasn't.

The real answer, as I see it, isn't "find a valuable skill and sell it to businesses." It's: find a thing you're good at and enjoy doing, and look for long-term ways to build assets (money is only one asset) from that golden combination of talent and passion that we all already have.

You'll still be working — maybe even harder than before — but it won't feel like a 9-to-5 grind anymore. And that's the difference.

I'm still working now, but it's so far outside what I'd call a "job" that I genuinely see it as my retirement activity for the rest of my time here.

All the best to everyone!
Want to escape work? Work harder. Brilliant!
How could you expect to get something unique (rare hack) from something trained on already established knowledge.
They’re so corporately limited frustratingly

Of course, if one loses the 9-5pm job, then what?  Here's my experience:  When doing the 9-5pm job, I am absolutely burned out with no energy or time left for anything else.  When I was younger, sure, I could do the regular job and work on the weekends, and I wish I had done this. The good news is by losing the salaried gig, a tremendous amount of physical and psychic energy is returned.  Plus, importantly, starting a 'path with a heart' is a huge morale booster, and since one now has the 'why' as to what I am living for, the interim work, such as consulting , is now tenable, as opposed to a fear based reaction to a crisis.

"Don't quit your job because you hate it.
Quit your job when it becomes unnecessary."
~ This is the message!
I am contractually prohibited by my 9-5 from starting a side business

Most of the employers I had a privilege and an extreme pleasure to work for explicitly state that I am not "allowed" to do anything else for money even during my own time. Justification is that I might get "exhausted" by making other income and it will affect my performance negatively.... Ain't that special? Another popular reason is "conflict of interest".

The reason you got the same answer wasn't because of some epiphany, it's because you asked the question in a way (i.e. lots of caveats and restrictions) that exposed the fact they were all trained on the same reference data
